question.text:
You are evaluating the financial performance of two retail chains based on their profitability ratios: Chain A: Return on Assets (ROA) = 10%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 15% Chain B: Return on Assets (ROA) = 12%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 18%
Assuming Chain A and Chain B have the same equity multiplier, which chain has a higher net profit margin?

answer.text: Both chains have the same net profit margin
Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: Since ROE = Net Profit Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier, if two firms have the same equity multiplier, the firm with higher ROE must have a higher margin × turnover. Chain B has ROE 18% vs Chain A's 15% (same multiplier assumed), and since ROA = Margin × Turnover and Chain B already has higher ROA (12% vs 10%), Chain B clearly has the higher net profit margin path. The Trap: Picking Chain A ignores the ROE gap; 'same margin' would only hold if ROE and ROA were identical; 'cannot determine' misreads the simplifying assumption about equal equity multipliers. Cross-Exam Context: DuPont-equivalent reasoning is tested in NISM XV, X-B, XXI-B and XIX-C/D for portfolio-company analysis. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Use the DuPont framework to explain to clients why two 'same ROE' companies are very different bets — one might run on margin, the other on turnover or leverage, and PMS risk differs accordingly.
